newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia July-Dec budget deficit A$9.082 bln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia July-Dec budget deficit A$9.082 bln.

text.p: Australia's underlying budget deficit for the six months to December, the first six months of fiscal 1996/97, was A$9.082 billion, compared with A$10.327 billion a year earlier, Finance Minister John Fahey said on Friday.
The headline balance was a A$5.198 billion deficit, compared with a A$5.306 billion deficit for the same period last fiscal year, Fahey said in a statement.
The underlying measure excludes the proceeds from asset sales and state government debt repayments.
Government finances are highly seasonal and cannot be extrapolated to estimate a final outcome for the fiscal year to June 30, 1997.
Revenue growth to December was 8.5 percent, compared with estimates in the August budget of 7.0 percent.
Outlays grew 7.6 percent, compared with budget projections of 2.4 percent, Fahey said.
Revenue growth was fuelled by an 8.5 percent increase in tax receipts over the same period in 1995/96.
The main increases in spending were in social security, and lower state government debt repayments.
The monthly headline balance for December was a A$3.334 billion credit compared with a credit of A$1.980 billion a year earlier.
The underlying balance was a A$3.405 billion credit, compared with a A$239 million credit in December 1995.
